validation.notes: Reads the resource panel, population, idle villagers, age and clock through cloud vision. Not yet checked against live captures at every UI scale; values the recogniser cannot read are left out, never guessed.

capture.notes: Use the default HUD at a UI scale where resource numbers are legible. Borderless window mode captures most reliably.

playerContext.help: When you aim to have reached the Feudal Age. 330 s (5:30) is a common starting point; good players are often near 4:00–5:00.

vision.purpose: Age of Empires IV. Read the resource panel (food, wood, gold, stone stockpiles; in the default layout it is at the bottom left, next to the number of workers on each), the population as current/maximum, the idle villager count if a number is shown, the current age (Dark, Feudal, Castle or Imperial; the age shown, not one being built), and the in-game clock. Report only numbers you can actually read. Report phase 'match_end' on a victory/defeat banner or the post-game summary, and 'menu' in menus, lobbies or loading screens.

concepts.title: Keep villagers coming
concepts.summary: Continuous villager production from the Town Center is the backbone of the economy. Every gap of 20 seconds is one villager you will never get back.
good: Rally new villagers straight onto a resource

concepts.title: Build houses before the cap
concepts.summary: Reaching the population cap stops all production. A house adds 10 population (5 for the Malians, who build them for half the cost; the Mongols need none).
good: Start a house a few population before the cap
bad: Hitting the cap and only then building

concepts.title: Age up on time, with the economy behind it
concepts.summary: You age up by building a landmark. Hitting your target time matters, but aging with too few villagers leaves you weak in the next age.
good: Plan the landmark and its villagers early
Keep producing villagers while the landmark builds
bad: Pulling every villager off resources to build

concepts.title: Spend what you gather
concepts.summary: Unspent resources do nothing. A large bank usually means a missing production building, upgrade or Town Center.
good: Add production when resources pile up

concepts.title: Scout, then react
concepts.summary: Knowing what the opponent is building lets you choose the right units and defences instead of guessing.
good: Scout early and again at each age-up
Build counter units to what you saw
bad: Massing one unit type without scouting

prohibitedAdvice: Anything about the opponent that is not visible on the player's own screen (fog of war, hidden armies)
Exploits, bugs or tools against the game's rules

terminology.housed: at the population cap, unable to make units
terminology.floating: holding a large unspent bank of resources

items.name: Version
items.detail: Update 17.0 shipped alongside the Raiders of the North expansion (preview posted Oct 22, 2026); it breaks older saves and replays and adds pause in single-player.

items.name: Raiders of the North
items.detail: Expansion adding the Vikings and Scots plus Crucible missions with co-op; released Oct 29, 2026 (unverified whether full or variant civilisations).

items.name: Recent expansions
items.detail: Yue Fei's Legacy (May 7, 2026: Jin Dynasty), Dynasties of the East (Nov 4, 2025: four variant civs and The Crucible), Knights of Cross and Rose (Apr 8, 2025), The Sultans Ascend (Nov 14, 2023).

items.name: Ranked season
items.detail: Season 14 runs Sep 1 to Nov 30, 2026 according to AoE4World (unverified officially).

items.name: Ranked 1v1 and Team Ranked
items.detail: Matchmade ranked play; new players play 5 placement matches.

items.name: Quick Match
items.detail: Unranked matchmaking including Empire Wars, Nomad and an 8-player free-for-all.

items.name: Empire Wars
items.detail: Starts with a developed economy, skipping the opening build order.

items.name: Nomad
items.detail: No starting Town Center; villagers start scattered and must found a base.

items.name: Single-player
items.detail: Campaigns, Historical Battles, Art of War challenges (bronze/silver/gold medals; the first is Early Economy), The Crucible, and skirmish against the AI.

items.name: Ranked map pool
items.detail: Rotates automatically every month since patch 16.3 (July 2026), mixing open, closed, hybrid and naval maps; read the map name from the loading screen.

items.name: Maps seen in past pools
items.detail: Dry Arabia, Sunkenlands, Rocky River, Archipelago, Socotra, Four Lakes, Golden Pit, Prairie, Hedgemaze, King of the Hill.

items.name: Loading screen
items.detail: Shows the map name and the civilisations of each player.

items.name: Post-game summary
items.detail: Victory or defeat screen, then a summary scoring Economy, Military, Technology and Society (community analysis, unverified).

items.name: Main menu
items.detail: Entry to Single Player, Multiplayer (Ranked, Quick Match, Custom), profile and settings.

items.name: Resources
items.detail: Bottom left in the default layout: food, wood, gold and stone, each with the number of villagers gathering it; hovering shows income per minute.

items.name: Minimap
items.detail: Lower left of the screen.

items.name: Idle villagers
items.detail: Period cycles idle economy units; Ctrl+Period selects all idle villagers (2021 defaults).

items.name: Population
items.detail: Shown as current/maximum; exact position unverified.

items.name: English
items.detail: Base game. Strong defensive economy and longbowmen.

items.name: French
items.detail: Base game. Cavalry-focused, strong early trade and royal knights.

items.name: Holy Roman Empire
items.detail: Base game. Prelates inspire villagers; strong infantry.

items.name: Mongols
items.detail: Base game. Nomadic; can pack up buildings; no houses needed.

items.name: Rus
items.detail: Base game. Earn gold from hunting; wooden fortresses.

items.name: Chinese
items.detail: Base game. Dynasties; tax collection; strong siege.

items.name: Delhi Sultanate
items.detail: Base game. Free technologies that take longer to research; war elephants.

items.name: Abbasid Dynasty
items.detail: Base game. House of Wisdom instead of landmarks for age-up wings.

items.name: Ottomans
items.detail: Free Anniversary update. Military schools produce units for free over time; Janissaries.

items.name: Malians
items.detail: Free Anniversary update. Pit mines; cheap houses that give 5 population.

items.name: Japanese
items.detail: The Sultans Ascend. Farmhouses instead of houses; samurai and onna-musha.

items.name: Byzantines
items.detail: The Sultans Ascend. Olive oil resource; mercenaries; cisterns.

items.name: Ayyubids
items.detail: Variant of the Abbasid Dynasty (The Sultans Ascend).

items.name: Jeanne d'Arc
items.detail: Variant of the French with a hero unit (The Sultans Ascend).

items.name: Order of the Dragon
items.detail: Variant of the Holy Roman Empire; Gilded Villagers cost 20% more and train in 23 s (The Sultans Ascend).

items.name: Zhu Xi's Legacy
items.detail: Variant of the Chinese (The Sultans Ascend).

items.name: Knights Templar
items.detail: Variant of the French (Knights of Cross and Rose).

items.name: House of Lancaster
items.detail: Variant of the English (Knights of Cross and Rose).

items.name: Golden Horde
items.detail: Variant of the Mongols (Dynasties of the East); starts with 200/200/150/50 stone.

items.name: Macedonian Dynasty
items.detail: Variant of the Byzantines (Dynasties of the East).

items.name: Sengoku Daimyo
items.detail: Variant of the Japanese (Dynasties of the East).

items.name: Tughlaq Dynasty
items.detail: Variant of the Delhi Sultanate (Dynasties of the East).

items.name: Jin Dynasty
items.detail: Variant of the Chinese (Yue Fei's Legacy, May 2026).

items.name: Vikings
items.detail: Raiders of the North (Oct 2026): Longhouse and Sagas mechanics; population cap can reach 210, or 220 with a cathedral technology.

items.name: Scots
items.detail: Raiders of the North (Oct 2026): a defensive civilisation.

items.name: Villager
items.detail: Costs 50 food and 1 population; trains in 20 seconds at the Town Center.

items.name: Standard start
items.detail: 6 villagers and 1 scout; generally 200 food, 150 wood, 100 gold (varies by civilisation).

items.name: Houses and population
items.detail: A house adds 10 population; the population cap is 200 for most civilisations.

items.name: Ages and landmarks
items.detail: Four ages (I Dark, II Feudal, III Castle, IV Imperial). Villagers build one of two landmarks per age to advance; each landmark gives a bonus.

items.name: Feudal Age cost
items.detail: About 400 food and 200 gold (unverified; varies by civilisation).

items.name: Typical Feudal timing
items.detail: Usually started a bit after 4:00; a consistent fast Feudal lands near 5:00 (community consensus).

items.name: Economy first
items.detail: Keep villager production continuous through the Castle Age; add Town Centers when you can afford them safely.

items.name: Scouting
items.detail: Scout the opponent's base early and after each age-up to choose the right units.

items.name: Counter units
items.detail: Spearmen beat cavalry, horsemen beat archers, archers beat spearmen, and men-at-arms and siege break defences.

items.name: Gaps in villager production
items.detail: Visible as an idle Town Center or a villager count that stalls.

items.name: Idle villagers
items.detail: The idle villager indicator shows a number; set rally points onto resources.

items.name: Floating resources
items.detail: The resource panel shows thousands banked; spend on production, upgrades or another Town Center.

items.name: Aging up too thin
items.detail: Reaching the next age with few villagers and no army to protect them.

items.name: Being housed
items.detail: Population equals the cap and production stops until a house finishes.

items.name: Boom
items.detail: Investing heavily in economy and extra Town Centers before building an army.

items.name: Fast castle
items.detail: Rushing to the Castle Age with a minimal army.

items.name: Tower rush
items.detail: Building towers near the opponent's resources early.

limitations: Reads only what the HUD shows; nothing hidden by the fog of war.
Frames are sampled every few seconds, so very short idle periods can be missed.
HUD positions and the civilisation list are researched, not yet checked against live captures at every UI scale.
Mistake durations are measured in real time on your screen.
failClosed: No cloud vision: this pack cannot read the game.
Numbers that cannot be read are left out, so no mistake is counted while the HUD is hidden or blurry.
